bib.title: Walking Down the Memory Maze: Beyond Context Limit through Interactive Reading

question: Can an LLM with a fixed context window read long text beyond its limit by navigating a tree of summaries as an interactive agent?
hypothesis: Treating the LLM as an interactive agent navigating a summary tree beats long-context windows, recurrence and retrieval on long inputs.
contributions: MemWalker: two-stage method (memory tree construction, navigation) via zero-shot iterative prompting
Outperforms recurrence, retrieval and full-context baselines on long-text QA, plus analysis of reasoning, working memory and error recovery

method.summary: Long text is split into segments, each summarised into leaf nodes, which are recursively summarised into a tree. At query time the LLM starts at the root, reasons over child summaries, picks a child or reverts to the parent, and answers at a leaf, carrying working memory from visited nodes.

datasets.name: QuALITY (SCROLLS)
datasets.source: Pang et al. 2022, Project Gutenberg stories

datasets.name: SummScreenFD (SCROLLS)
datasets.preprocessing: Repurposed: 'who' question generated from ground-truth summary with Stable Beluga 2, answers checked by a human expert

datasets.name: GovReport (SCROLLS)
datasets.preprocessing: Repurposed to QA the same way as SummScreenFD

other.note: base LLM for most experiments; finetuning does not overlap evaluation tasks

inference.decoding: top-p sampling for tree construction and for navigation reasoning/action
inference.prompting: Zero-shot, no fine-tuning or few-shot examples; triage prompt at non-leaf nodes, leaf prompt at leaves; unparsable output regenerated, three consecutive failures return 'no answer'
inference.retrieval: Baseline only: Contriever, top segments concatenated until context full

parameters.working memory: content of visited nodes, truncated to fit the context window

other.fig5 sweep: QuALITY, max children 2/4/8/16, 500 vs 1000-token segments (read from Fig 5)

metrics.name: valid action
metrics.definition: percent of generated actions that are a valid navigation action

metrics.name: stray ratio
metrics.definition: percentage of paths that contain the revert action

metrics.name: recovery rate
metrics.definition: percentage of stray paths that recover and answer correctly

baselines: Full context keep left / keep right (4,096 tokens)
eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; no seeds, variance or significance test stated.

availability.data: SCROLLS public; repurposed SummScreenFD/GovReport QA sets not stated as released

prompts.text: [TEXT OF SEGMNET]. Summarize the above text comprehensively into a fluent passage.
[SUMMARIES]. Compress each summary into a much shorter summary.

The following passage(s) are the summaries of the different parts of a story.
To answer the question: [QUERY]
Which of the following summary is MOST LIKELY to contain information about the answer?
First provide reasoning to compare the summaries before you make the decision.
Summary 0: [CHILD SUMM NODE 0]
Summary 1: [CHILD SUMM NODE 1]
...
Summary N: [CHILD SUMM NODE N]
Relpy with the passage number as your action.
You MUST choose one summary number and you should reply with the following format:
###################################
Reasoning: ...
Action: 0 / 1 / 2, ...
###################################

Read the text in triple quotes and answer a question:
Story background information: [WORKING MEMORY]
Main text: [TEXT OF SEGMNET]
[QUERY]
[OPTIONS]
If the answer CANNOT be inferred from the text above, reply with action -1. (Table 1/6 versions)
If the answer CAN be inferred from the text above, reply with action -2, and also provide your reasoning, and the final answer.
You are ONLY allowed to reply with action -2 or -1.
Your should reply with the following format:
###################################
Reasoning: ...
Action: -2 or -1
Answer: ...
###################################

limits: Tree construction may not scale to extremely long sequences (authors).
Needs a strong reasoning LLM, over 70B and instruction-tuned; 13B models failed (authors).
Tree-building cost (calls, tokens, time) not reported; top-p, temperature and max tokens not stated; single run per cell with no variance.
Long-subset sizes not stated (Fig 2 says buckets of equal size); SummScreenFD/GovReport QA sets are synthetic, generated by Stable Beluga 2, which is also the evaluated model.
Working memory is truncated, not summarised (footnote).
